clue.text: Hear MP's not changed communication device

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the three words before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An MP's speech has stayed the same, overheard and passed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' shuffles HEARMPSNOT into the gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone with computing functions is a device people use to communicate.

clue.text: Reprimand Cairo poet appearing regularly in court

indicators.note: in places the alternate letters inside the abbreviation for court
appearing regularly picks every other letter of the words Cairo poet, starting with the second

explanation.surface: An Egyptian poet keeps turning up at a royal court or in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of CAIRO POET give ARPE, which goes between C and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is an informal British verb for summoning them to be told off, as onto the boss's carpet.

clue.text: Traffic system upset club visiting outskirts of Grimsby

indicators.note: visiting puts the reversed club inside the outer letters, as a guest goes in
outskirts of takes only the outside letters of the town name Grimsby
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: the Rotary is a well-known service club

explanation.surface: A club's tour bus is overturned on a roundabout on the edge of the fishing town of Grimsby.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the club upside down. Grimsby is an English port town in Lincolnshire; Rotary is an international service club.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyratory is a British term for a large one-way circulatory road system, a kind of roundabout.

clue.text: Compose a sonata piece that's mellow

indicators.note: a piece of the phrase is a run of its letters taken from inside it

explanation.surface: A composer is urged to write a gentle, mellow sonata.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' signals letters hidden across composE A SONata; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to mature or soften over time, as timber or wine does with age.

clue.text: English student fills up Bordeaux in wine cabinet

indicators.note: fills up means the first pair of letters goes inside the wine, filling it

parts.note: claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine
L is the learner, the student driver of British L-plates

explanation.surface: An English student tops up the Bordeaux kept in a cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fills up' puts EL inside CLARET, after its C. Learner drivers in Britain show an L-plate, hence L for student.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a sideboard or cabinet for storing bottles of wine in a dining room.

clue.text: Flimsy fabric

definitions.meaning: flimsy as in a weak, unconvincing excuse
a cloth woven with metallic gold or silver threads

explanation.definitionFit: A weak excuse is lame, and lamé is a glittering fabric with metal threads.

clue.text: Reportedly warm and sunny? It's brief!

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for warm and sunny is said, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: weather that is warm and sunny is summery, like high summer

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster delivers a short, cheerful forecast for a fine day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns SUMMERY into its sound-alike; 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary dismissal or judgment is a brief one, done without formality or delay.

clue.text: Resolute quality of head chasing dates around hurriedly

indicators.note: chasing means coming after the other parts, as a pursuer follows
around means the letters of dates are moved about

parts.note: dates gives letters to be rearranged
hurriedly means fast, quickly
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A headteacher rushes after the diary dates, in a determined frame of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a person but is a headland, as in Scottish place-names; 'around' scrambles the dates and 'chasing' puts the headland last.
explanation.definitionFit: Being steadfast is being firm and unwavering, so the noun names resolution as a quality.

clue.text: Green leader prepared to admit source of money

indicators.note: to admit means the anagram lets the letter in, enclosing it
prepared means the letters of leader are made ready in a new arrangement
source of takes the first letter, where money starts

explanation.surface: A Green Party leader gets ready to declare where the party's money came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' turns LEADER into EERALD and 'to admit' puts M inside after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green colour, named after the green gemstone.

clue.text: Flight of criminal pair and escape

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, set in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Two crooks flee from custody together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges PAIRANDESCAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight is running away or vanishing from a place, as a fugitive does, so a vanishing act fits.

clue.text: Ethnic grouping comprising half of Greece's constituents?

parts.note: the letters that make up the word Greece are G, R, E, E, C, E: half of them are E, the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A demographer asks about a group making up half of Greece's people.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'constituents' as the letters of GREECE, three of six are E, which stands for European; the Greeks themselves are also Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of a whole continent form a broad grouping by origin and culture.

clue.text: City detectives could be seeking them, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is said aloud to give a word sounding the same

parts.note: detectives follow up leads, pieces of evidence to pursue

explanation.surface: Police in a city are on the trail of clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns LEADS into the Yorkshire city that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Drank to excess back in warehouse

indicators.note: back means the word for drank heavily is read the other way

parts.note: toped is an old word for drank heavily, as a toper does

explanation.surface: Someone drank too much back at the warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TOPED; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse where goods or vehicles are kept.

clue.text: Title of private vessel the Queen goes aboard

indicators.note: goes aboard means getting on the vessel, inside the private ship

parts.note: own means private, belonging to oneself
a ship is a sea vessel
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: The Queen boards a private yacht, which carries a title.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's usual Queen. 'Title' here is the legal sense, not a name or rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Title in law is the right of possession, legal proof that something belongs to you.

clue.text: Hard rock yielding lead, maybe

definitions.meaning: a loud, aggressive style of rock music
lead is one example of a dense element of high atomic weight

explanation.surface: A rock face produces lead ore for the miners.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a loud rock-music genre and a dense element such as lead or mercury.

clue.text: In haughty manner, is it an indication toilet needs cleaning?

parts.words: is it an indication toilet needs cleaning?
parts.note: the question pictures an insect buzzing about a lavatory, a sign the bathroom wants a scrub

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a stand-offish manner shows the bathroom is dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A LOO FLY: a fly in the toilet hints that it needs cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and superior, so acting that way is behaving haughtily.

clue.text: Was originator of one-time TV sitcom?

indicators.note: one-time read as one T, time, means only one of the two T letters is kept

parts.note: Father Ted was a British TV sitcom about Irish priests

explanation.surface: A quiz question asks who created an old television comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted (1995-98) is a Channel 4 sitcom; 'one-time' says to keep just one of its two T's (T is time).
explanation.definitionFit: To father something is to create or originate it, as a man begets a child.

clue.text: Power failure crossing river creates shock

indicators.note: crossing means the power failure spans the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: an outage is a loss of electricity supply
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A blackout spreads across a river and causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts R inside OUTAGE; 'creates' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is anger and shock at something offensive.

clue.text: Left by pier, bananas past sell-by date?

parts.note: left over means remaining, so left gives over

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of pier go wild

explanation.surface: Bananas left by a pier have gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges PIER into RIPE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit too ripe is beyond its best, like food past the date shops must sell it by.

clue.text: Score with ace in card game

parts.note: a score is twenty
an ace is the one in a suit of cards

explanation.surface: A player wins points by holding an ace during a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon or blackjack is played aiming for a hand totalling this number, and is named after it.

clue.text: Courses of some interest I brought up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards
some means only part of the letters of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: A student's courses were chosen from some of the interests brought along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes STIBRO from intereST I BROught; 'up' reverses it. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbits are the paths that planets and satellites take, so they are courses.

clue.text: Head of council, stable occupant it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the horse word is pronounced to give a sound-alike

parts.note: a mare is a female horse, which lives in a stable

explanation.surface: A council leader is spoken of as a horse in its stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' makes MARE sound like the civic title in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A town or city council is chaired by its civic leader, who holds this title.

clue.text: Male attending annual Royal occasion displays charm

parts.note: Royal Ascot is a yearly race meeting attended by the royal family

explanation.surface: A man at Royal Ascot shows off a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is a fashionable June horse-race meeting in Berkshire. 'attending' and 'displays' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is an object or figure thought to bring good luck, a charm.

clue.text: Avoid opening press release put out

indicators.note: put out means the press release letters are thrown out of the opening

parts.note: a prelude is an opening piece or introduction
PR, public relations, deals in press releases

explanation.surface: A spokesman dodges the start of a press release being issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' removes PR from the front of PRELUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to escape or dodge something, as a fugitive avoids capture.

clue.text: Fruit crop each year from Puglia

indicators.note: crop means to cut away, so letters are trimmed off the place name

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: A grower harvests fruit every year from the Italian region of Puglia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop' trims P and A from PUGLIA; 'from' is a link. 'crop' looks like a harvest noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Swiss location's extremely tolerable home for composer

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital; with the possessive it gives Bern's

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters, the extremes, of tolerable

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A Swiss town is described as a fairly agreeable place for a composer to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives TE from tolerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein was the American composer of West Side Story.

clue.text: Striking entails getting beaten up

indicators.note: getting beaten up means the letters of entails are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking part in a strike leads to being assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting beaten up' rearranges ENTAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature stands out and is conspicuous, so it is striking.

clue.text: Inclined to defend footballers being vulgar

indicators.note: to defend means wrapping round the footballers, guarding them

parts.note: prone means inclined or liable to
FA is the Football Association, the body of English football

explanation.surface: Footballers being crude are inclined to stick up for each other.
explanation.walkthrough: FA is England's Football Association; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane language is irreverent or coarse, so vulgar.
